title: A repeated operation is idempotent rather than cumulatively additive
summary: A narrow operation model says applying the same operation twice to the same state yields the same result as once; a cumulative model predicts a second measurable change.

design.unit: paired records or repeated operation frames with the same input/state
design.prediction: When the same operation is repeated without an intervening state change, the second output should equal the first; a cumulative operation should expose a second increment or distinct result marker.
design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial repetition could generate the same surface pattern without the proposed operation rule.
design.falsifier: A repeated operation changes the state again under the same input and no intervening operation, or an intervening change is required to produce the observed difference.
design.principal_risk: Independent operation identity and state measurements are missing. Near quantity scaling and identity persistence, but the discriminator is repeat application under unchanged input.
